sections.h2: What should you know about Stanly County property tax?
sections.html:
Stanly County bills property tax through one office, Stanly County Tax Administration, which values property, sends bills and collects. The county covers 395 square miles and holds more than 42,000 parcels and has ten municipalities, according to its mapping office.

The Census Bureau puts the July 1, 2025 population at 68,830, up 10.1% from the 2020 base. Most homes here are owner-occupied, so property tax touches most households. If you plan to sell, the points that matter are the January 1 valuation date, the September bill, the tax certification needed to record a deed, and any relief you used that may come due.

  • Values are set as of January 1, and the bill follows the owner of record on that date.
  • The county rate and each town's rate are applied to that value, then special charges such as the fire district and solid waste fee are added.
  • A deed cannot be recorded until the county certifies that no delinquent tax is owed.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers show for Stanly County?
sections.html:
Stanly County is a low-density county of owner households. The 2020-2024 Census figures show a 74.5% owner-occupied rate, a median owner-occupied home value of $242,400 and median gross rent of $861, with 25,240 households averaging 2.49 people.

Some 20.3% of residents are 65 or older, and median household income is $60,704. The Census Bureau counted 336 building permits in 2025 and 29,780 housing units in July 2025. New construction is one reason an assessed value can change between revaluations.

sections.h2: Who do you contact at Stanly County Tax Administration?
sections.html:
The department sits in the Stanly County Courthouse at 201 South Second Street in Albemarle and is open Monday through Friday, 8:30 am to 5 pm. The county merged its tax collector's and tax assessor's offices into one department in the spring of 2008.

It has three divisions with separate jobs. The Real Property Division appraises all real property at its market value as of the latest reappraisal. The Personal Property Division lists and audits boats, aircraft, untagged vehicles and business equipment and prepares the annual bills. The Tax Collector's Division collects county, municipal, fire district and special district taxes.

  • Collections, first floor, Room 104: 704-986-3619.
  • Real and personal property, second floor: 704-986-3626.
  • Mapping and land records, 1000 North First Street, Suite 20: 704-986-3637.

sections.h2: When are Stanly County tax bills sent, and what changed for 2026?
sections.html:
Bills arrive in late July or early August. The county says its tax rate did not change for 2026 and that none of its municipalities changed theirs. One fire district, Aquadale, moved its rate from 10 to 12 cents, and the yearly solid waste fee stayed at $99. Check the 2026 rate page or ask the tax office for the rate that applies to your address, since your bill depends on your town and fire district.

State law makes tax due September 1 and payable at face value until early January, with interest of 2% for the first month of delinquency and three-quarters of one percent for each month after. Personal property follows a different timetable, with listing in January: the county begins taking listings on January 2, the last day is January 31, and a 10% late-listing penalty applies after that.

Per the county, tax cannot be prorated for individual personal property other than registered motor vehicles. The assessment reflects the property's status as of January 1.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Stanly County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with an informal appeal with the Tax Administrator's office, then go to the Board of Equalization and Review if you still disagree. The county says the 2026 appeal window has closed, and the next one is the 2027 assessment, with informal appeals requested before May 1, 2027. Appeals registered after that date may have to be heard formally by the board.

The county's revaluation guide says an informal review is a meeting with a certified appraiser, and you need proof of your opinion such as recent sales or an appraisal. A response of too high is not a valid explanation. You may also appeal by mail with a copy of your notice and a daytime phone number to the Tax Assessor at 201 South Second Street. The county describes the Board of Equalization and Review as five members appointed by the commissioners. After it rules, the next steps are the North Carolina Property Tax Commission in Raleigh and then the courts.

Market changes since the last reappraisal date of January 1, 2025 cannot be considered until the next one, which the county schedules for January 1, 2029. For personal property, the county says to appeal within 30 days of the bill date.

sections.h2: What tax relief programs exist in Stanly County?
sections.html:
The county lists three homestead programs and a present-use program for working land. An owner who qualifies for more than one may take only one. Applications run from January 2 to June 1.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: removes the greater of $25,000 or 50% of the value of a permanent residence. The county prints a $39,900 income limit for 2027 applications based on 2026 income. Applicants must be at least 65 or totally and permanently disabled, and a married applicant counts both spouses' income.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: excludes the first $45,000 of value. The surviving unmarried spouse can qualify. A form certifying the disability from the VA must accompany it.
  • Circuit breaker deferment: limits tax to 4% of income, or 5% in the higher band up to $59,850, and defers the rest. The owner must have lived in the home five full years. Deferred tax for the current year and three prior years becomes a lien and is due with interest if the owner transfers the home, dies or stops using it as a residence.

Present-use value taxes farmland and forest by its use rather than market value. Agriculture needs at least ten acres in commercial production, horticulture five acres, forestry twenty acres with a written management plan, and wildlife land twenty to one hundred acres. Selling or changing the use of such land can end the benefit, so ask the tax office about any back tax before signing a contract.

sections.h2: What must happen at closing when you sell in Stanly County?
sections.html:
Before a deed can be recorded, a Tax Certification Form must be completed. You fill in the top portion, the assessor or mapping office completes the middle, and the Tax Collector certifies that no delinquent tax is owed and stamps the deed so that the Register of Deeds can record it. Plan for this step if you are closing on a deadline.

The seller pays the state's deed excise tax of $1.00 for each $500 of consideration, collected by the register of deeds before recording. Standard recording fees are $26 for the first 15 pages and $64 for a deed of trust, with $4 per added page. Current-year tax is normally prorated between buyer and seller, so ask your closing attorney to show the figure and pay the bill from proceeds.

A house sold with back tax can also be sold as-is to a cash buyer, who pays the balance at closing. The lien on the parcel attaches as of the listing date, and a tax foreclosure action can follow if the bill stays unpaid.

faqs.q: Where is the Stanly County tax office?
faqs.a: It is in the Stanly County Courthouse at 201 South Second Street, Albemarle, NC 28001, open Monday through Friday from 8:30 am to 5 pm. Collections is on the first floor in Room 104 at 704-986-3619.

faqs.q: When is the next Stanly County revaluation?
faqs.a: The county schedules the next one for January 1, 2029. The latest took effect January 1, 2025. Under state law each county must reappraise at least every eight years.

faqs.q: Can I get my deed recorded if taxes are delinquent?
faqs.a: No. The Tax Collector must certify that no delinquent tax is owed on the Tax Certification Form and stamp the deed before it goes to the Register of Deeds. Pay the balance first.

faqs.q: How do I apply for the elderly or disabled exclusion in Stanly County?
faqs.a: File Form AV-9 with the tax office between January 2 and June 1, with proof of income. A disability claim needs a physician's certificate on Form AV-9A. The county prints the income limit for 2027 applications as $39,900.

faqs.q: Do I owe tax on personal property if I sell my house?
faqs.a: Personal property such as boats and untagged vehicles is listed each January and assessed as of January 1. The county says it cannot prorate it except for registered vehicles. Selling the house does not erase a listing already due.
